questions.q: What did Malcolm's childhood experiences produce in him?
a: A determination to fight for justice and fair treatment of black people
A desire to leave the United States permanently
A distrust of all forms of education
A plan to become a lawyer
questions.why: Lesson 1 traces his commitment to justice to his father's death, his mother's hospitalization and school prejudice.

questions.q: What does the summary say prison did for Malcolm?
a: It gave him time to read, learn about Islam and become a speaker
It convinced him that crime was his only option
It separated him from his family forever
It taught him a trade he used later
questions.why: Lesson 2 says prison was the path to becoming who he was meant to be, through reading and debate.

questions.q: Why did Malcolm break with the Nation of Islam?
a: He learned its leader had betrayed his trust, and later questioned his own beliefs
He was offered a leadership role elsewhere
He disagreed with its stance on education
He wanted to enter politics directly
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes his disillusionment with Elijah Muhammad and the doubts that followed his pilgrimage.

questions.q: What did Malcolm's pilgrimage to Mecca show him?
a: Kindness among Muslims of all races, which made him reconsider his views
That religious rituals were unnecessary
That he should retire from activism
That America had solved its racial problems
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the hospitality he met from people of every heritage forced him to second-guess himself.

questions.q: What lesson does the summary draw from Malcolm admitting he was wrong?
a: It is never too late to admit error and change for the better
Public figures should never admit mistakes
Only young people can change their views
Apologies cannot repair a reputation
questions.why: Lesson 3 ends by saying it is never too late to admit you were wrong and change.
